messages.author: 2167f025066e0cf4
messages.subject: DIC in Besag model
parts:
I am trying to compare models with and without spatial random effects using DIC to see whether it would be sufficient to fit models without the spatial effects (because of the long run time and memory issues). However, I don't get a DIC value in the summary of the model with the spatial effects. If I look at results$dic, I get this output:

$dic
[1] NaN

$p.eff
[1] NaN

$mean.deviance
[1] NaN

$deviance.mean
[1] 20694.15

$family.dic
[1] NA

$family.p.eff
[1] NA

Compared to the same model without the spatial effects:

$dic
[1] 32161.11

$p.eff
[1] 4536.927

$mean.deviance
[1] 27624.18

$deviance.mean
[1] 23087.26

$family.dic
[1] 32161.11

$family.p.eff
[1] 4536.927

Does anyone have any ideas about why this might be happening and whether there is a way to calculate DIC for the model with spatial effects?

Thanks,
Adam Green

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] DIC in Besag model
parts:
You need to tell it to compute it.

result = inla(formula, family=...,data, ... , control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))

Check out ?control.compute for other things that are optional.

D
